notes.content: Harbor ingests partner CSV files from an SFTP drop every night at 02:00 UTC.
Harbor's transformation layer is written in dbt and executed by Airflow.
The warehouse behind Harbor is Snowflake, in the EU-West region.
Harbor's CI runs dbt build against a small sample dataset in a Snowflake dev schema.
Priya Natarajan is the on-call engineer for Harbor during the first two weeks of each month.
Marco handles on-call for Harbor in the second half of each month.
Decision on 2025-12-15: Harbor will not use Spark, since the data volumes stay below 50 GB per day and dbt is sufficient.
Incident on 2026-01-08: the nightly load failed because a partner changed the CSV delimiter from comma to semicolon without notice. The loader now sniffs the delimiter.
Harbor's Airflow DAGs must set retries to 3 with exponential backoff; never use fixed delays.
The postmortem owner for incidents in Harbor is whoever was on call at the time.
Data quality checks in Harbor use Great Expectations, run after every dbt model build.
All Harbor tables containing personal data are tagged pii and must be masked in the staging environment.
The Harbor staging environment is refreshed from production snapshots every Wednesday.
Alerts from Harbor go to the #harbor-alerts channel; severity one pages the on-call via PagerDuty.
Harbor does not retain raw partner files longer than 400 days because of the contractual retention limit.
Marco prefers pairing sessions over written design docs for small Harbor changes.
Harbor's orchestration moved from Airflow 2.6 to Airflow 2.9 on 2026-03-30 to get dataset-aware scheduling.
Snowflake costs for Harbor were reduced by 30 percent after switching the warehouse size from Large to Medium on 2026-04-07.
Dashboards for Harbor are built in Metabase and read only from the marts schema.
Because the Medium warehouse is slower, the month-end aggregation job in Harbor now runs at 22:00 UTC instead of 02:00 UTC.
Priya's on-call rotation for Harbor was changed on 2026-05-05: she now covers the last two weeks of each month, and Marco covers the first two.
Harbor secrets are stored in AWS Secrets Manager and rotated every 90 days.
The Harbor team standup is at 09:30 CET on weekdays.
Gotcha: the dbt incremental model for orders silently drops late-arriving rows older than 3 days unless the lookback window is increased.
Harbor's SFTP drop moved from a self-hosted server to AWS Transfer Family on 2026-06-09, after the old server's disk failed.
Convention: every new Harbor dbt model needs a description and at least one uniqueness test on its primary key.
Harbor row counts are compared against partner-supplied manifests; a mismatch greater than 0.5 percent blocks the load.
The Harbor data catalog is DataHub; owners must be filled in for every dataset.
Harbor's CSV loader processes files in parallel with a maximum of 8 workers.
The Great Expectations suite for orders was extended on 2026-07-28 to also check currency codes against ISO 4217.
Decision on 2026-08-04: Harbor adopts Iceberg tables for the raw layer because they allow schema evolution without rewrites.
Priya Natarajan is presenting the Harbor architecture at the internal data guild on 2026-09-15.
Cost alert: Snowflake credits for Harbor exceeded the monthly budget of 800 credits in August 2026, mostly due to a runaway backfill.
On 2026-09-01 the partner Acme started sending files gzip-compressed; the loader handles .gz transparently.
Harbor's SLA: data must be available in the warehouse by 07:00 UTC on business days.
Marco is on parental leave from 2026-10-01 until 2027-01-15, so Priya covers all Harbor on-call during that time.
The data guild meets on the first Tuesday of every month.
Acme is a partner that sends order files; Globex sends inventory files.
Backfills in Harbor must be run on the XS warehouse and approved by the on-call engineer.
Harbor's retention limit for raw partner files was reduced from 400 days to 365 days on 2026-09-29.
